chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who said:

I asked him and said: 'If I am on the road to Mecca and leave the prayer in places where there are Bedouins, should I perform the obligatory prayer on the ground and recite only the Opening of the Book, or should I pray on the mount and recite the Opening of the Book and the chapter?' He said: 'When you fear, pray on the mount the obligatory and non-obligatory prayers. If you recite the Praise and a chapter, it is more beloved to me, and I do not see any harm in what you have done.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer while traveling if fearing attack or danger?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the flexibility of *Salat al-Musafirin* (traveler's prayer) when fear of Bedouin raids necessitates praying on one's mount. While the scholar prefers the complete recitation of *Al-Fatiha* and a *Surah*, he explicitly validates praying with only *Al-Fatiha* as sufficient, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease (*taysir*) in times of danger. This ruling underscores the distinction between the obligatory minimum and the recommended completeness in ritual performance under duress.
